intended_object: The inverse system (diagram) of the finite p-group quotients G/U of a profinite group G. It is indexed by the open normal subgroups U for which G/U is a p-group, ordered by inclusion, with the natural projections G/U → G/V when U ≤ V. Its limit is the maximal pro-p quotient. This is read off the docstring and from how the library uses it (`diagram`, `product`).
explanation:
The index category is `Quotient p G`: open normal subgroups U of G such that G/U is a p-group, with the partial order lifted from `OpenNormalSubgroup`. The relevant source of the structure is in the definition's file, `ProfiniteGroups/ProP.lean`. A morphism U ⟶ V is an inclusion U ≤ V. The functor sends U to the finite group G/U. It sends a morphism U ⟶ V to the projection G/U → G/V, built as `QuotientGroup.map` of the identity on G. This is exactly the standard inverse system of finite p-quotients, so the definition matches the docstring.

It also matches Mathlib's `ProfiniteGrp.toFiniteQuotientFunctor : OpenNormalSubgroup P ⥤ FiniteGrp`, which has the same `obj` and `map`. The only difference is that this diagram restricts the indexing to the p-quotient kernels. Mathlib does not define this restricted diagram or the maximal pro-p quotient, so there is no exact counterpart.

The generality is natural: it works for any prime p and any profinite group G in any universe. The `Fact p.Prime` hypothesis is standard for pro-p constructions and does not restrict the object in any meaningful way. Degenerate cases also behave correctly: the trivial quotient G/G is always included as the top element.
